title: Drishyam 3: The Conclusion Opens to Rs 95.1 Crore Worldwide, Bollywood's Second-Biggest 2026 Debut
excerpt: Ajay Devgn's franchise finale collected an estimated Rs 66.75 crore net in India on day one, just shy of the Rs 100-crore debut mark but the second-highest Bollywood opening of 2026.
body:
• Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3: The Conclusion, released October 2, 2026, collected an estimated ₹66.75 crore net in India and ₹95.10 crore gross worldwide on its opening day, per Sacnilk estimates reported by Filmibeat.
  • The split: India gross ₹80.10 crore, overseas ₹15 crore, across 15,759 shows. Hindi 2D occupancy averaged 67.08%, climbing from 46.38% in the morning to 76.46% at night.
  • It is the second-highest Bollywood opener of 2026, behind Dhurandhar 2, and it topped the opening-day figures of both franchise predecessors.
  • Reader utility: this is the Hindi concluding chapter starring Ajay Devgn — not the Malayalam Drishyam 3 (Mohanlal), which released earlier in 2026 and is a different film; the Hindi version opened after 4.05 lakh advance tickets were sold, the 7th-biggest Indian pre-sale on record.

Opening news lead

The Salgaonkar saga has ended with a thunderclap. Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3: The Conclusion opened to an estimated ₹95.10 crore worldwide on its first day of release, October 2, 2026, falling just short of the ₹100-crore debut mark but establishing itself as the second-biggest Hindi opener of the year, according to trade tracker Sacnilk's data reported by Filmibeat.

https://x.com/taran_adarsh/status/2105664856284414457

The India numbers are formidable on their own: ₹66.75 crore net across 15,759 shows, translating to a gross of ₹80.10 crore, with overseas markets contributing a further ₹15 crore. Audience momentum built through the day — the Hindi 2D version's occupancy rose from 46.38% in morning shows to 70.15% in the afternoon, 75.31% in the evening, and 76.46% at night.

Context & Background

The franchise's day-one dominance has a pattern. Trade reports note the concluding chapter surpassed the opening-day collections of both Drishyam and Drishyam 2, the Hindi remakes that turned the Malayalam thriller template into one of Bollywood's most reliable brands. Strong advance bookings — 4.05 lakh tickets sold before release, the seventh-biggest pre-sale ever for an Indian film — set the stage.

The film also cleared its regulatory path cleanly: the Central Board of Film Certification passed it with zero cuts, and it released with a 150-minute runtime. Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar, the cable-operator-turned-mastermind whose battle of wits with the police defined the first two chapters.

Impact & Analysis

The opening lands as a franchise statement. At a time when big Hindi releases have struggled for consistency in 2026, a mid-budget thriller with an 11-year-old lead character outperforming most star vehicles validates the franchise's loyal-audience model. Filmibeat's assessment — "heavy audience interest and strong franchise recall" — is visible in the evening occupancy surge, which suggests walk-in business beyond the pre-booked core.

The ₹95.10 crore figure also resets expectations for the conclusion's full run. The second-highest opener of 2026 sits behind only Dhurandhar 2, and with the opening weekend still to play out, trade analysts will watch whether the film converts the goodwill of the franchise finale into sustained holds.

Diaspora Angle

The ₹15-crore overseas day-one haul underscores the diaspora's box-office muscle. Gulf, North American, and UK audiences have long treated the Drishyam franchise as appointment viewing, and the concluding chapter's first-day international pull shows the Indian diaspora remains the decisive swing audience for big Hindi releases.

What's Next / Looking Ahead

All eyes are on the opening weekend. With the film's night-show trajectory pointing up and the franchise's word-of-mouth historically strong, the question is how far past the ₹95-crore start the first three days can carry it — and whether the concluding chapter can finish as the definitive commercial peak of the Salgaonkar story.
